diagnostic_evidence.quote:
u^*(t)
            =   \eexp^{-itH} u_0 - i \int_0^t \diff s \eexp^{-i(t-s)H} (f(s) - B(s) u^*(s))

issues.failure_explanation: The equation implies (i\partial_t-H)u=f+Bu, so variation of constants gives an integrand f+Bu, not f-Bu. The displayed formula and the fixed-point map instead solve (i\partial_t-H+B)u=f.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace f-Bu by f+Bu in the Duhamel and fixed-point formulas and adjust the immediately associated sign computations.
issues.overall_effect: The Duhamel assertion in Proposition 2.1 is false for nonzero B, and the appendix's existence proof constructs the solution with the opposite sign of B.
issues.title: Wrong sign for the time-dependent perturbation in the Duhamel formula
issues.why_classification: This is a forced local sign repair; the contraction and energy arguments otherwise remain valid and all stated existence and continuity guarantees survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: F(v) = \abs{v(0) - u_0}^2 + T \norm{(i\partial_t - \eexp^{itH_0} (A + B(t)) \eexp^{-itH_0}) v - \eexp^{itH_0} f}_{\Ltwosp{I, \HHilb}}^2
Let \fctshortdef{B}{t \in \setclosure I}{B(t)} be a strongly continuous family of bounded self-adjoint operators on $\HHilb$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof computes the residual for A alone and identifies f with (i\partial_t-H)u*, although the stated equation has H+B(t) and the functional contains A+B(t). Thus the displayed identity F(v)=||u-u*||² does not follow from the calculation as written when B is nonzero.

failure_location.quote:
(i\partial_t - \eexp^{itH_0} A \eexp^{-itH_0}) v - \eexp^{itH_0} f
            &=	i\partial_t \eexp^{itH_0} u - \eexp^{itH_0} A u - \eexp^{itH_0} f

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert B(t) together with A throughout the residual computation and use f=(i\partial_t-H-B(t))u*.
issues.overall_effect: The principal coercivity and equivalence claim of the corollary is left unproved for the advertised time-dependent bounded perturbation.
issues.title: Proof of the transformed variational formulation drops B(t)
issues.why_classification: The omitted bounded term can be restored by a short local calculation without changing the statement, constants, or proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Since H=H0+A, the definition gives S*=S0*-(A+B), with A+B interpreted as the induced antidual operator. The proposition states a plus sign, contradicting both the defining residual i\partial_t-H0-A-B and the later identity used in Corollary 3.3.

failure_location.quote:
\adjoint S u = (\adjoint S_0 + A + B(t)) u
                = i \delta_0 \otimes u_0 + f
failure_location.tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace S0*+A+B by S0*-(A+B) and replace the corresponding Id-plus formula by Id-(S0*)^{-1}(A+B).
issues.overall_effect: The asserted operator equivalence and the displayed preconditioned equation in Proposition 3.4 are false as written.
issues.primary_affected_tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.title: The dual perturbation operator has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: The source itself uses the correct minus sign later, so a forced local sign correction restores the operator identity without mathematical loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
E^*(u)
            =	\norm{u(t) + i \int_0^t \diff s \eexp^{-i(t-s)H_0}(Au) - \left( \eexp^{-itH_0} u_0 - i \int_0^t \diff s \eexp^{-i(t-s)H_0} f(s) \right)}_{\Ltwosp{I, \HHilb}}^2

issues.failure_explanation: The converse proof replaces the defining test operator i\partial_t-H-B(t) by i\partial_t-H, so the displayed equality is false when B is nonzero. The resulting L2 functional likewise contains only Au, although the section and the claimed target equation include B(t)u.

failure_location.tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain B(t) in the converse argument and replace every occurrence of Au in the dual least-squares perturbation by (A+B(t))u, with the corrected operator sign.
issues.overall_effect: The converse PDE characterization is unsupported for nonzero B, and Corollary 3.3's functional generally minimizes the equation without B rather than the stated time-dependent equation.
issues.primary_affected_tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.title: The dual formulation repeatedly omits the bounded perturbation B(t)
issues.why_classification: Once the omitted bounded term is restored, the same duality and coercivity argument applies and the advertised scope is preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The operator $A$ is a closed symmetric operator on $\HHilb$ such that $D(H_0) \subset D(A)$.
Using a slight abuse of notation, we also denote the multiplication operator $A$ by $V$.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the paper's assumptions A need not be bounded and Au is not defined for an arbitrary u in L2(I,H). Consequently the displayed Bochner integral and hence E*(u) are not literally defined on the claimed whole space. The proof implicitly needs a bounded extension of (S0*)^{-1}A obtained through an antidual pairing, but no such extension or interpretation of the integral is defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define A from L2(I,H) into the antidual of Y_H0 by duality against A applied to test functions, prove this map and (S0*)^{-1}A are bounded, and state that the integral denotes that extension; alternatively restrict the domain, at the cost of losing the claimed L2 formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed globally defined strongly convex L2 functional is ill-posed in the principal Coulomb/unbounded-potential regime.
issues.title: The L2 dual functional is not defined for a general unbounded A
issues.why_classification: Preserving the full L2 domain requires a contained but nontrivial operator-extension argument and a revised definition, rather than a routine notation change.

issues.failure_explanation: The left side of the theorem is the global C0(R,L2) supremum norm and therefore does not depend on t, whereas the proof establishes only the pointwise bound ||(i\partial_t)^{k+1}v*(t)||≤Ck(1+|t|^{k/2})||u0||. For k>0 the latter allows polynomial growth and does not establish membership of the derivative in bounded C0(R,L2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the global C0 norm in the estimate by the pointwise L2 norm at time t, or use an explicitly weighted C0 norm encoding the proved polynomial growth.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's global-in-time uniform derivative estimate is unsupported; only continuity together with polynomial pointwise growth is established.
issues.title: The time-regularity theorem states a global norm where only a pointwise growth estimate is proved
issues.why_classification: The repair materially weakens a global uniform estimate to a polynomial-growth estimate, although the regularity conclusion and spectral-method motivation remain comparable.
